statement: For either signed complete Collatz inverse operator, every r>=0 and every unit residue a modulo 3^(r+1), and every real H and natural cutoffs D,B, there exist d>=D and a positive odd integer m>=B in that residue with K_d(m)>H. The same quantified assertion holds for the all-source coefficient C_d. The proof transports the actual one-halving coefficient spike through a fixed exponent branch, using powers-of-two coverage of all ternary units. The integer target may depend on depth; neither fixed-integer coefficient-series divergence nor an infinite integer escape trajectory is proved.
